Job Story

The Department of Economics in the W. Frank Barton School of
Business invites applications for a Senior Educator position in
Economics to begin in the fall of 2027.

Candidates will teach courses at the undergraduate and graduate
levels using various instructional delivery formats, including
traditional face-to-face, hybrid, blended, and fully online
instruction. The position will foster applied learning in course
design and engage with industry and the local business community
through applied projects. The successful candidate will also
advance knowledge through scholarly activities, including active
involvement in committees, student mentorship, recruitment and
retention initiatives, and outreach activities.

We are looking for an instructor who can teach undergraduate- and
graduate-level courses such as Behavioral Economics. They will
establish clear learning objectives, develop curriculum and
instructional materials that accomplish those objectives, and
provide students with the support needed to succeed.

Wichita State University places applied learning at the center of
student experience. Every degree program at Wichita State includes
a guaranteed applied learning or research experience, providing
students with opportunities to develop relevant professional skills
and meaningful experience before graduation. The successful
candidate will have opportunities to integrate these experiences
into economics education through applied projects with industry and
engagement with local businesses and the larger community. The
department provides undergraduate and graduate economics education
and creates opportunities for teaching, applied learning,
interdisciplinary collaboration, and engagement with industry and
the broader community.

Job Summary

Teach courses at the undergraduate and graduate levels using
various instructional deliveries (e.g., traditional (face-to-face),
hybrid, and fully online). To foster applied learning into the
course design and engage with industry and local business community
applied projects. To advance knowledge through scholarly activities
(e.g., active involvement in committees, student mentorship,
recruitment and retention initiative, outreach activities,
etc.)

Essential Functions

Meet expectations for teaching and service, as set forth by the
department and college.

Job Duties

The successful candidate will be expected to:
1. Teaching: Teach four courses in the fall semester and four
courses in the spring semester. Each course is three credit hours,
with 2.5 hours of class time per week. Classes will be taught at
the undergraduate and graduate levels using face-to-face and other
instructional modalities, including online and blended
formats.

2. Course Design and Student Support: Establish key objectives for
classes; create curriculum that accomplishes the established
objectives; develop syllabi that outline the topics to be explored
and list due dates for assignments and examinations; give lectures
and organize activities to present material and deepen
understanding of coursework; and answer students’ questions and
provide support to help them succeed.

3. Applied Learning and Community Engagement: Engage with local
businesses and the larger community to provide applied-learning
opportunities for students through industry- and community-based
projects.

4. Service and Scholarly Activities: Engage in service activities
at the department, Barton School of Business, university,
profession, and local community levels. Scholarly activities may
include active involvement in committees, student mentorship,
recruitment and retention initiatives, and outreach
activities.

Required Education and Experience:

Graduate level degree or Equivalent Experience in the
Field
Teaching experience

Faculty Requirements

A graduate-level degree or higher in Economics or closely
related field, at the time of application.
For degrees in a related field, direct experience within the
field of economics.
Teaching experience at any level.

Knowledge, Skills and Abilities:

Evidence of technical and soft skills
Knowledge of Behavioral Economics, statistics, and principles
of microeconomics and macroeconomics.
Ability to build professional relationships within the
community and across the university at all levels.
Ability to provide instruction of curriculum to a variety of
learners.
Commitment to collaborative processes and environments.

Additional Information:

WSU is not able to provide immigration sponsorship for this
position.
